claim: BMP signaling has a conserved function in patterning the dorsal-ventral body axis in Bilateria and the directive axis in anthozoan cnidarians.
source: BMP signaling has a conserved function in patterning the dorsal-ventral body axis in Bilateria and the directive axis in anthozoan cnidarians.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature establishing this conservation.

claim: The directive body axis of Nematostella vectensis appears at gastrula stage.
source: In contrast to Bilateria, where the D-V axis and the A-P axis usually form simultaneously and very early during development, the directive body axis of the sea anemone Nematostella vectensis appears only at gastrula stage (Matus et al., 2006a; Matus et al., 2006b; Rentzsch et al., 2006), while the O-A axis is maternally determined (Lee et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies (Matus et al., 2006a; Matus et al., 2006b; Rentzsch et al., 2006).

claim: The O-A axis in Nematostella is maternally determined.
source: In contrast to Bilateria, where the D-V axis and the A-P axis usually form simultaneously and very early during development, the directive body axis of the sea anemone Nematostella vectensis appears only at gastrula stage (Matus et al., 2006a; Matus et al., 2006b; Rentzsch et al., 2006), while the O-A axis is maternally determined (Lee et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2007.

claim: During gastrulation, the Nematostella embryo undergoes a BMP signaling-dependent symmetry break establishing the directive axis at a molecular level.
source: During gastrulation, the embryo undergoes a BMP signaling-dependent symmetry break establishing the directive axis at a molecular level (Rentzsch et al., 2006; Saina et al., 2009), with a BMP signaling activity gradient forming as revealed by antibody staining against phosphorylated SMAD1/5 (pSMAD1/5) (Figure 1C and D; Genikhovich et al., 2015; Leclère and Rentzsch, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations (Rentzsch et al., 2006; Saina et al., 2009) and by reference to Figure 1C and D showing pSMAD1/5 staining.

claim: A BMP signaling activity gradient forms during gastrulation as revealed by antibody staining against phosphorylated SMAD1/5.
source: During gastrulation, the embryo undergoes a BMP signaling-dependent symmetry break establishing the directive axis at a molecular level (Rentzsch et al., 2006; Saina et al., 2009), with a BMP signaling activity gradient forming as revealed by antibody staining against phosphorylated SMAD1/5 (pSMAD1/5) (Figure 1C and D; Genikhovich et al., 2015; Leclère and Rentzsch, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations (Genikhovich et al., 2015; Leclère and Rentzsch, 2014) and by Figure 1C and D showing pSMAD1/5 staining patterns.

claim: bmp2/4 and chordin are expressed on the low BMP signaling activity side of the directive axis.
source: Each end of the directive axis expresses a set of BMP ligands and BMP antagonists: bmp2/4 and bmp5-8 are transcribed on the low BMP signaling activity side of the directive axis together with the antagonist chordin, while the BMP ligand gdf5-like (gdf5-l) and the BMP antagonist gremlin are expressed on the high BMP signaling activity side (Genikhovich et al., 2015; Rentzsch et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Genikhovich et al., 2015 and Rentzsch et al., 2006.

claim: bmp5-8 is transcribed on the low BMP signaling activity side of the directive axis.
source: Each end of the directive axis expresses a set of BMP ligands and BMP antagonists: bmp2/4 and bmp5-8 are transcribed on the low BMP signaling activity side of the directive axis together with the antagonist chordin, while the BMP ligand gdf5-like (gdf5-l) and the BMP antagonist gremlin are expressed on the high BMP signaling activity side (Genikhovich et al., 2015; Rentzsch et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Genikhovich et al., 2015 and Rentzsch et al., 2006.

claim: gdf5-like and gremlin are expressed on the high BMP signaling activity side of the directive axis.
source: Each end of the directive axis expresses a set of BMP ligands and BMP antagonists: bmp2/4 and bmp5-8 are transcribed on the low BMP signaling activity side of the directive axis together with the antagonist chordin, while the BMP ligand gdf5-like (gdf5-l) and the BMP antagonist gremlin are expressed on the high BMP signaling activity side (Genikhovich et al., 2015; Rentzsch et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Genikhovich et al., 2015 and Rentzsch et al., 2006.

claim: Chordin likely acts as a shuttle for BMP2/4/BMP5-8.
source: The pSMAD1/5 gradient is maintained by the genetic interactions between these molecules, with Chordin likely acting as a shuttle for BMP2/4/BMP5-8 and Gremlin serving as a primary GDF5-like antagonist (Genikhovich et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Genikhovich et al., 2015.

claim: Gremlin serves as a primary GDF5-like antagonist.
source: The pSMAD1/5 gradient is maintained by the genetic interactions between these molecules, with Chordin likely acting as a shuttle for BMP2/4/BMP5-8 and Gremlin serving as a primary GDF5-like antagonist (Genikhovich et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Genikhovich et al., 2015.

claim: rgm is necessary for the maintenance of the low BMP signaling side of the directive axis.
source: Another essential player in this network is the repulsive guidance molecule (rgm), which is necessary for the maintenance of the low BMP signaling side of the directive axis (Leclère and Rentzsch, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Leclère and Rentzsch, 2014.

claim: Complete abolishment of the BMP signaling gradient by KD of bmp2/4, bmp5-8, or chordin results in embryos that are molecularly and morphologically radialized, failing to form any mesenteries.
source: More specifically, complete abolishment of the BMP signaling gradient by KD of bmp2/4, bmp5-8, or chordin results in embryos which are not only molecularly but also morphologically radialized, failing to form any mesenteries (Genikhovich et al., 2015; Leclère and Rentzsch, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Genikhovich et al., 2015 and Leclère and Rentzsch, 2014.

claim: KD of gdf5-l or gremlin alter the profile of the BMP signaling gradient and lead to abnormal mesentery formation.
source: In line with this, KD of gdf5-l or gremlin alter the profile of the BMP signaling gradient and lead to abnormal mesentery formation (Genikhovich et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Genikhovich et al., 2015.

claim: 91 significant ChIP peaks corresponding to 68 direct pSMAD1/5 target genes were found at late gastrula stage.
source: We found 91 significant ChIP peaks corresponding to 68 direct pSMAD1/5 target genes at late gastrula stage and 282 significant ChIP peaks corresponding to 208 pSMAD1/5 target genes in 4d planulae, 24 of which were bound by pSMAD1/5 at both developmental stages (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by the ChIP-seq data presented in the manuscript and shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: 282 significant ChIP peaks corresponding to 208 pSMAD1/5 target genes were found in 4d planulae.
source: We found 91 significant ChIP peaks corresponding to 68 direct pSMAD1/5 target genes at late gastrula stage and 282 significant ChIP peaks corresponding to 208 pSMAD1/5 target genes in 4d planulae, 24 of which were bound by pSMAD1/5 at both developmental stages (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by the ChIP-seq data presented in the manuscript and shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: 24 genes were bound by pSMAD1/5 at both late gastrula and 4d planula developmental stages.
source: We found 91 significant ChIP peaks corresponding to 68 direct pSMAD1/5 target genes at late gastrula stage and 282 significant ChIP peaks corresponding to 208 pSMAD1/5 target genes in 4d planulae, 24 of which were bound by pSMAD1/5 at both developmental stages (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by the ChIP-seq data presented in the manuscript and shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: 49 out of 91 late gastrula ChIP peaks were located within previously published Nematostella enhancers.
source: In total, 49 out of 91 late gastrula and 67 out of the 282 4d planula ChIP peaks were located within the previously published Nematostella enhancers (Schwaiger et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with previously published enhancers (Schwaiger et al., 2014).

claim: 67 out of 282 4d planula ChIP peaks were located within previously published Nematostella enhancers.
source: In total, 49 out of 91 late gastrula and 67 out of the 282 4d planula ChIP peaks were located within the previously published Nematostella enhancers (Schwaiger et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with previously published enhancers (Schwaiger et al., 2014).

claim: The BMP response element (BRE) sequence was enriched at many of the pSMAD1/5 bound sites.
source: MEME-ChIP analysis (Ma et al., 2014) of the sequences occupied by pSMAD1/5 showed that the BMP response element (BRE) sequence, a vertebrate SMAD1/5 binding motif, was enriched at many of the bound sites.
evidence: This is supported by MEME-ChIP analysis of the ChIP-seq data.

claim: Most genes identified as pSMAD1/5 targets at both stages carry a BRE motif (22/24).
source: Most genes identified as pSMAD1/5 targets at both stages carry a BRE motif (22/24), with 13 additional gastrula-specific targets and 20 additional 4d planula-specific targets containing a BRE site (Figure 1E, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by motif analysis of the ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: 13 additional gastrula-specific targets contain a BRE site.
source: Most genes identified as pSMAD1/5 targets at both stages carry a BRE motif (22/24), with 13 additional gastrula-specific targets and 20 additional 4d planula-specific targets containing a BRE site (Figure 1E, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by motif analysis of the ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: 20 additional 4d planula-specific targets contain a BRE site.
source: Most genes identified as pSMAD1/5 targets at both stages carry a BRE motif (22/24), with 13 additional gastrula-specific targets and 20 additional 4d planula-specific targets containing a BRE site (Figure 1E, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by motif analysis of the ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: gbx, hoxB, hoxD, and hoxE are direct pSMAD1/5 targets.
source: These included gbx, hoxB, hoxD, and hoxE, that is, genes shown to play a central role in the subdivision of the directive axis into mesenterial chambers and specifying the fate of each mesenterial chamber (He et al., 2018), as well as the BMP signaling regulators chordin, gremlin, and rgm (Genikhovich et al., 2015; Leclère and Rentzsch, 2014; Saina et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by the ChIP-seq data and citations to He et al., 2018.

claim: chordin, gremlin, and rgm are direct pSMAD1/5 targets.
source: These included gbx, hoxB, hoxD, and hoxE, that is, genes shown to play a central role in the subdivision of the directive axis into mesenterial chambers and specifying the fate of each mesenterial chamber (He et al., 2018), as well as the BMP signaling regulators chordin, gremlin, and rgm (Genikhovich et al., 2015; Leclère and Rentzsch, 2014; Saina et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by the ChIP-seq data and citations to Genikhovich et al., 2015; Leclère and Rentzsch, 2014; Saina et al., 2009.

claim: None of the BMP ligand-coding genes (bmp2/4, bmp5-8, or gdf5-like) were found among the direct BMP signaling targets.
source: Intriguingly, none of the BMP ligand-coding genes, that is, bmp2/4, bmp5-8, or gdf5-like, were found among the direct BMP signaling targets (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by the ChIP-seq data presented in Supplementary file 1.

claim: 139 direct pSMAD1/5 target genes were differentially expressed in the KD (padj≤0.05).
source: In total, 139 direct pSMAD1/5 target genes were among the genes differentially expressed in the KD (padj≤0.05), 64 of which showed more than a twofold change in expression upon BMP2/4 and/or GDF5-like KD (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data comparing morpholino knockdowns.

claim: 64 direct pSMAD1/5 target genes showed more than a twofold change in expression upon BMP2/4 and/or GDF5-like KD.
source: In total, 139 direct pSMAD1/5 target genes were among the genes differentially expressed in the KD (padj≤0.05), 64 of which showed more than a twofold change in expression upon BMP2/4 and/or GDF5-like KD (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data comparing morpholino knockdowns.

claim: chordin and rgm were upregulated in BMP2/4 and GDF5-like KD.
source: The transcriptional response of the previously described downstream targets of BMP signaling confirmed previous in situ hybridization analysis, that is, chordin and rgm were upregulated while gbx, hox genes and gremlin were downregulated in our RNA-seq datasets confirming their specificity.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data from morpholino knockdowns.

claim: gbx, hox genes and gremlin were downregulated in BMP2/4 and GDF5-like KD.
source: The transcriptional response of the previously described downstream targets of BMP signaling confirmed previous in situ hybridization analysis, that is, chordin and rgm were upregulated while gbx, hox genes and gremlin were downregulated in our RNA-seq datasets confirming their specificity.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data from morpholino knockdowns.

claim: Out of 55 pSMAD1/5 target genes with BRE motifs, 37 (67.3%) were differentially expressed upon BMP2/4 and/or GDF5-like KD.
source: Notably, out of 55 pSMAD1/5 target genes with BRE motifs, 37 (67.3%) were shown to be differentially expressed upon BMP2/4 and/or GDF5-like KD (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by combined ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: The fraction of transcription factors and signaling molecules was strongly increased among the direct BMP signaling targets at both developmental stages in comparison to 100 randomly selected genes from the Nematostella genome.
source: We found that the fraction of TFs and SMs was strongly increased among the direct BMP signaling targets at both developmental stages in comparison to 100 randomly selected genes from the Nematostella genome (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: This is supported by functional annotation analysis shown in Figure 1F and G.

claim: Several newly identified pSMAD1/5 targets are bilaterally expressed (e.g., otxB, tbx2/3, tbx20.1, p63, dusp1, bmprII, c-ski, morn, pik, zswim4-6).
source: In accordance with a potential role in the directive axis regulation, we found several of the newly identified pSMAD1/5 targets to be bilaterally expressed (e.g., otxB, tbx2/3, tbx20.1, p63, dusp1, bmprII, c-ski, morn, pik, zswim4-6) (Figure 2), further motivating the investigation of their function in directive axis patterning.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2.

claim: 103 direct BMP signaling targets were conserved between at least two organisms (Nematostella, Drosophila, Xenopus).
source: We found 103 direct BMP signaling targets that were conserved between at least two organisms, of which four were shared by all three species (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is supported by comparative analysis of ChIP-seq data from three species shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: Four direct BMP signaling targets were shared by all three species (Nematostella, Drosophila, Xenopus).
source: We found 103 direct BMP signaling targets that were conserved between at least two organisms, of which four were shared by all three species (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is supported by comparative analysis of ChIP-seq data from three species shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: At least eight targets can be assigned to all three species (meis, gata, tbx2/3, nkain, irx, zfp36l1, ptc, tp53bp2) based on two-way reciprocal best BLAST hits.
source: Analyzing the targets in Nematostella with two-way reciprocal best BLAST hits to targets in Drosophila or Xenopus suggests that a total of at least eight can be assigned to all three species (meis, gata, tbx2/3, nkain, irx, zfp36l1, ptc, tp53bp2).
evidence: This is supported by bioinformatic analysis of orthology relationships.

claim: Among the shared targets, conserved transcription factors and signaling molecules are enriched compared to genes with other functions (69/103).
source: Among the shared targets, conserved TFs and SMs are enriched compared to genes with other functions (69/103).
evidence: This is supported by functional annotation of conserved targets.

claim: Multiple Hox genes are direct targets of BMP signaling in embryos of Nematostella (hoxB, hoxD, hoxE), fly (dfd, pb, antp), and frog (hoxa1-7/9-11/13, hoxb1-9, hoxc3-6/8-12, hoxd1/3/4/8-11/13).
source: Multiple Hox genes are direct targets of BMP signaling in embryos of Nematostella (hoxB, hoxD, hoxE), fly (dfd, pb, antp), and frog (hoxa1-7/9-11/13, hoxb1-9, hoxc3-6/8-12, hoxd1/3/4/8-11/13); however, the orthology of the cnidarian and bilaterian Hox genes is unclear due to the likely independent diversification of the 'anterior' and 'non-anterior' Hox genes in these two sister clades (Chourrout et al., 2006; Genikhovich and Technau, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data from three species and citations to Chourrout et al., 2006; Genikhovich and Technau, 2017.

claim: zswim4-6 is a pSMAD1/5 target shared between Nematostella and Xenopus.
source: One of the highest enrichment levels in our ChIP-seq was detected for zswim4-6 – a pSMAD1/5 target shared between Nematostella and Xenopus (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Nematostella ZSWIM4-6 clusters together with ZSWIM4/5/6 of zebrafish, frog, and mouse.
source: This gene encodes a zinc-finger containing protein with a SWIM-domain clustering together with ZSWIM4/5/6 of zebrafish (Danio rerio), frog (Xenopus tropicalis), and mouse (Mus musculus) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: zswim4-6 starts to be expressed at the early gastrula stage around the blastopore.
source: Zswim4-6 starts to be expressed at the early gastrula stage around the blastopore (Figure 4B–C'), concomitant with the onset of BMP signaling activity.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 4B–C'.

claim: At late gastrula, zswim4-6 expression becomes restricted to the ectoderm and endoderm on one side of the directive axis.
source: At late gastrula, when a symmetry break in the BMP signaling activity establishes the directive axis, zswim4-6 expression becomes restricted to the ectoderm and endoderm on one side of it (Figure 4D and D').
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 4D and D'.

claim: zswim4-6 is expressed opposite to chd, on the side of high pSMAD1/5 activity.
source: Double in situ hybridization of chd and zswim4-6 shows that zswim4-6 is expressed opposite to chd, that is, on the side of high pSMAD1/5 activity (Figure 4E and E'), suggesting that BMP signaling activates zswim4-6 expression.
evidence: This is supported by double in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 4E and E'.

claim: At late planula stage, strong zswim4-6 expression is observed in the eight mesenteries.
source: At late planula stage, strong zswim4-6 expression is observed in the eight mesenteries (Figure 4F and F').
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 4F and F'.

claim: Full-length ZSWIM4-6-EGFP is translocated into the nuclei.
source: Full-length ZSWIM4-6-EGFP was enriched in the cell nuclei (Figure 4G), while the truncated version of ZSWIM4-6 lacking the NLS remained cytoplasmic, similar to the EGFP signal in transgenic animals overexpressing only cytoplasmic EGFP (Figure 4H and I).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: ZSWIM4-6ΔNLS-EGFP missing the predicted nuclear localization signal remains cytoplasmic.
source: Full-length ZSWIM4-6-EGFP was enriched in the cell nuclei (Figure 4G), while the truncated version of ZSWIM4-6 lacking the NLS remained cytoplasmic, similar to the EGFP signal in transgenic animals overexpressing only cytoplasmic EGFP (Figure 4H and I).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: The nuclear fluorescent signal of ZSWIM4-6-EGFP progressively decreases from early blastula to 24 hpf.
source: Strikingly, the nuclear fluorescent signal of ZSWIM4-6-EGFP, which is weak but clearly visible at the early blastula stage (Figure 4J), progressively decreases and is barely detectable at 24 hpf (Figure 4K).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 4J and K.

claim: Injection of mRNA encoding cytoplasmic EGFP results in a strong fluorescent signal lasting for several days.
source: In contrast, injection of mRNA encoding cytoplasmic EGFP results in a strong fluorescent signal lasting for several days (Figure 4L).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 4L.

claim: The KDs of bmp2/4 and chd led to a loss of zswim4-6 expression.
source: In line with the proposed role of BMP signaling in activating zswim4-6 expression, the KDs of bmp2/4 and chd led to a loss of zswim4-6 expression (Figure 5B–D', Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 5B–D'.

claim: KD of gdf5-like and gremlin did not strongly affect zswim4-6 expression.
source: In contrast, KD of gdf5-like and gremlin did not strongly affect zswim4-6 expression (Figure 5E and F', Supplementary file 1), suggesting that zswim4-6 expression might either specifically depend on the BMP2/4-mediated, but not GDF5-like-mediated BMP signaling, or be robust toward milder alterations in pSMAD1/5 levels, or both.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 5E and F'.

claim: Both Alk2 and Alk3/6 had to be knocked down in order to abolish zswim4-6 transcription.
source: On the contrary, both Alk2 and Alk3/6 had to be knocked down in order to abolish zswim4-6 transcription, suggesting that in our developmental context, Alk2 and Alk3/6 may need to heterodimerize to transduce BMP signal, similar to the situation reported in zebrafish (Tajer et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by receptor knockdown experiments and citation to Tajer et al., 2021.

claim: zswim4-6 KD leads to defects in endoderm compartmentalization.
source: Analysis of the overall morphology at late planula stage showed that zswim4-6 KD leads to defects in endoderm compartmentalization.
evidence: This is supported by morphological analysis of morphants.

claim: In ZSWIM4-6MO, the mesenterial chamber expressing HoxE protein failed to reach the pharynx, resulting in the fusion of the two neighboring mesenterial segments.
source: In contrast, in ZSWIM4-6MO, the mesenterial chamber expressing HoxE protein failed to reach the pharynx, resulting in the fusion of the two neighboring mesenterial segments (Figure 6B and B').
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6B and B'.

claim: zswim4-6 morphant primary polyps formed only three instead of the typical four tentacles.
source: Consequently, zswim4-6 morphant primary polyps formed only three instead of the typical four tentacles (Figure 6B'').
evidence: This is supported by morphological analysis shown in Figure 6B''.

claim: The gradient profile of pSMAD1/5 in the endoderm was flattened in zswim4-6 morphants compared to controls.
source: We found that the gradient profile of pSMAD1/5 in the endoderm was flattened in zswim4-6 morphants compared to controls, and that peak levels of pSMAD1/5 activity were not reached.
evidence: This is supported by quantification of pSMAD1/5 immunofluorescence.

claim: pSMAD1/5 activity in the ectoderm was strongly elevated upon zswim4-6 KD.
source: pSMAD1/5 activity in the ectoderm was, however, strongly elevated upon zswim4-6 KD (Figure 6C–C' and D–D').
evidence: This is supported by quantification of pSMAD1/5 immunofluorescence shown in Figure 6C–C' and D–D'.

claim: zswim4-6 mRNA overexpression did not result in significant changes in the shape of the pSMAD1/5 gradient in the endoderm.
source: zswim4-6 mRNA overexpression did not result in significant changes in the shape of the pSMAD1/5 gradient in the endoderm; however, ectodermal pSMAD1/5 levels were significantly reduced in the area where BMP signaling is normally strongest (Figure 6E–E' and F–F').
evidence: This is supported by quantification of pSMAD1/5 immunofluorescence shown in Figure 6E–E' and F–F'.

claim: Ectodermal pSMAD1/5 levels were significantly reduced in the area where BMP signaling is normally strongest upon zswim4-6 mRNA overexpression.
source: zswim4-6 mRNA overexpression did not result in significant changes in the shape of the pSMAD1/5 gradient in the endoderm; however, ectodermal pSMAD1/5 levels were significantly reduced in the area where BMP signaling is normally strongest (Figure 6E–E' and F–F').
evidence: This is supported by quantification of pSMAD1/5 immunofluorescence shown in Figure 6E–E' and F–F'.

claim: Overexpression of zebrafish zzswim5 affects the pSmad1/5/9 gradient in zebrafish embryos.
source: The expansion of the pSMAD1/5 domain upon Nematostella zswim4-6 KD and its reduction upon zswim4-6 overexpression suggests that SMAD1/5 may be stabilized in the absence of ZSWIM4-6. This is in line with the effect of the overexpression of zebrafish zzswim5 on the pSmad1/5/9 gradient in zebrafish embryos (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), as well as with the recently reported role of the vertebrate Zswim4 in frog embryos and mammalian cells (Wang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Adding ZSWIM4-6MO to the GDF5lMO led to a much milder reduction of the pSMAD1/5 gradient compared to GDF5lMO alone.
source: As we showed previously (Genikhovich et al., 2015), pSMAD1/5 staining was drastically reduced upon GDF5lMO injection, but adding ZSWIM4-6MO to the GDF5lMO indeed led to a much milder reduction of the pSMAD1/5 gradient (Figure 6—figure supplement 3), supporting the ZSWIM4-6-mediated pSMAD1/5 destabilization hypothesis.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: The bmp2/4, chd, and rgm expression domains were expanded in zswim4-6 morphants compared to controls.
source: The bmp2/4, chd, and rgm expression domains were expanded in zswim4-6 morphants compared to controls (Figure 6G–H', Figure 6—figure supplement 4), which was especially evident in the ectodermal expansion of chd and rgm.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6G–H' and Figure 6—figure supplement 4.

claim: The chd expression domain was expanded in mosaic F0 zswim4-6 knockouts generated by CRISPR/Cas9.
source: Similarly, the chd expression domain was also expanded in the mosaic F0 zswim4-6 knockouts generated by CRISPR/Cas9, corroborating the morpholino KD results (Figure 6—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 5.

claim: The KD of zswim4-6 translation resulted in a strong upregulation of zswim4-6 transcription, especially in the ectoderm.
source: The KD of zswim4-6 translation resulted in a strong upregulation of zswim4-6 transcription, especially in the ectoderm, suggesting that ZSWIM4-6 might either act as its own transcriptional repressor or that zswim4-6 transcription reacts to the increased ectodermal pSMAD1/5 (Figure 6I and I').
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6I and I'.

claim: The expression domain of gdf5-like was expanded in the ectoderm in zswim4-6 morphants.
source: The expression domain of gdf5-like (Figure 6J and J') and grm (Figure 6K and K') was expanded in the ectoderm, which reflects the flattening of the endodermal and the expansion of the ectodermal pSMAD1/5 gradient in the morphants (Figure 6C–D').
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6J and J'.

claim: The expression domain of grm was expanded in the ectoderm in zswim4-6 morphants.
source: The expression domain of gdf5-like (Figure 6J and J') and grm (Figure 6K and K') was expanded in the ectoderm, which reflects the flattening of the endodermal and the expansion of the ectodermal pSMAD1/5 gradient in the morphants (Figure 6C–D').
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6K and K'.

claim: zswim4-6-egfp overexpression caused a mild reduction of the expression domains of bmp2/4 and chd.
source: As expected from the analysis of the morphants, zswim4-6-egfp overexpression caused a mild reduction of the expression domains of bmp2/4 and chd (Figure 6L–M').
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6L–M'.

claim: The otherwise very sharp border of the chd expression domain appeared diffuse upon zswim4-6-egfp overexpression.
source: Moreover, the otherwise very sharp border of the chd expression domain appeared diffuse (Figure 6M').
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6M'.

claim: gdf5-like expression appeared reduced on the 'strong gdf5-like side' upon zswim4-6-egfp overexpression.
source: gdf5-like expression (Figure 6O and O') appeared reduced on the 'strong gdf5-like side', and grm was reduced as well (Figure 6P and P'), which also reflects the behavior of the pSMAD1/5 gradient (Figure 6F and F').
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6O and O'.

claim: grm expression was reduced upon zswim4-6-egfp overexpression.
source: gdf5-like expression (Figure 6O and O') appeared reduced on the 'strong gdf5-like side', and grm was reduced as well (Figure 6P and P'), which also reflects the behavior of the pSMAD1/5 gradient (Figure 6F and F').
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6P and P'.

claim: The pSMAD1/5 binding site-containing region at the chordin locus was 1.82-fold enriched upon anti-GFP-ChIP in EF1α::ZSWIM4-6-EGFP embryos.
source: On the other hand, the pSMAD1/5 binding site-containing region at the chordin locus was 1.82-fold enriched upon anti-GFP-ChIP in EF1α::ZSWIM4-6-EGFP embryos and 0.15-fold enriched (significant according to the two-tailed t-test; p=0.00032) in wild-type embryos (Figure 6Q).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6Q.

claim: The pSMAD1/5 binding site-containing region at the gremlin locus was depleted in both wild type and in EF1α::ZSWIM4-6-EGFP-injected embryos upon αGFP-ChIP.
source: The pSMAD1/5 binding site-containing region at the gremlin locus was depleted in both wild type and in EF1α::ZSWIM4-6-EGFP-injected embryos upon αGFP-ChIP (0.35-fold enrichment and 0.27-fold enrichment, respectively; not significant according to the two-tailed t-test; p=0.496).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data.

claim: The enrichment of the pSMAD1/5 binding site-containing region at the chordin locus in EF1α::ZSWIM4-6-EGFP embryos in relation to wild-type embryos was 12.13-fold.
source: Thus, the enrichment of the pSMAD1/5 binding site-containing region at the chordin locus in EF1α::ZSWIM4-6-EGFP embryos in relation to wild-type embryos was 12.13-fold, in stark contrast to the 0.87-fold enrichment at the gremlin locus in EF1α::ZSWIM4-6-EGFP embryos in comparison to the wild-type embryos.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data.

claim: ZSWIM4-6 interacts with the pSMAD1/5 binding site of the chordin regulatory region, but not of the gremlin regulatory region.
source: This suggests an interaction of ZSWIM4-6 with the pSMAD1/5 binding site of the chordin regulatory region, but not of the gremlin regulatory region, and supports the hypothesis that ZSWIM4-6 might act as a co-repressor for pSMAD1/5 targets.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential ChIP enrichment at chordin vs gremlin loci.

claim: Functional annotation of the identified pSMAD1/5 targets highlights an abundance of transcription factors and signaling molecules.
source: Functional annotation of the identified targets highlights an abundance of TFs and SMs (Figure 1F), suggesting that BMP signaling regulates a second tier of regulators rather than structural genes at the two stages we assayed.
evidence: This is supported by functional annotation analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claim: BMP signaling regulates a second tier of regulators rather than structural genes at late gastrula and 4d planula stages.
source: Functional annotation of the identified targets highlights an abundance of TFs and SMs (Figure 1F), suggesting that BMP signaling regulates a second tier of regulators rather than structural genes at the two stages we assayed.
evidence: This is inferred from the functional annotation showing enrichment of regulatory genes.

claim: The presence of multiple members of Wnt, MAPK, Hedgehog, and Notch signaling pathways among the BMP signaling targets points at a high degree of coordination between different signal transduction cascades.
source: The presence of multiple members of Wnt, MAPK, Hedgehog, and Notch signaling pathways among the BMP signaling targets points at a high degree of coordination between different signal transduction cascades necessary to generate a properly organized embryo.
evidence: This is inferred from the identification of multiple signaling pathway components as BMP targets.

claim: pSMAD1/5 in Nematostella directly controls the transcription of multiple BMP network components (chd, grm, bmprII, rgm, smad1/5, smad4) and other associated regulators (e2f4, morn, tob2, c-ski, tld1-like, bmp1-like, dusp1, dusp7).
source: Likewise, pSMAD1/5 in Nematostella directly controls the transcription of multiple BMP network components (chd, grm, bmprII, rgm, smad1/5, smad4) and other associated regulators (e2f4, morn, tob2, c-ski, tld1-like, bmp1-like, dusp1, dusp7) that have not been characterized yet.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data identifying these genes as direct targets.

claim: The promoters of Nematostella BMP-encoding genes do not appear to be directly bound by pSMAD1/5.
source: Curiously, unlike Xenopus bmp2, -4, -5, -7, and gdf2, -6, -9, and -10, or Drosophila dpp (Deignan et al., 2016; Stevens et al., 2017), the promoters of Nematostella BMP-encoding genes do not appear to be directly bound by pSMAD1/5.
evidence: This is supported by the absence of these genes in the ChIP-seq data and comparison with other species (Deignan et al., 2016; Stevens et al., 2017).

claim: BMP signaling-dependent repression of Nematostella bmp2/4 and bmp5-8, and BMP signaling-dependent activation of gdf5-like is indirect.
source: Our ChIP-seq data suggest that BMP signaling-dependent repression of Nematostella bmp2/4 and bmp5-8, and BMP signaling-dependent activation of gdf5-like (Genikhovich et al., 2015) is indirect, but the link between the pSMAD1/5 activity and the transcriptional regulation of BMPs is still unknown.
evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq data showing no direct binding of pSMAD1/5 to BMP ligand genes.

claim: The endodermal BMP-dependent staggered expression of hox genes and gbx is directly controlled by nuclear pSMAD1/5.
source: Our ChIP-seq analysis showed that the endodermal BMP-dependent staggered expression of hox genes and gbx is directly controlled by nuclear pSMAD1/5.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data showing direct binding of pSMAD1/5 to hox genes and gbx.

claim: RNAi of hoxE, hoxD, hoxB, or gbx led to the loss of the pairs of mesenteries corresponding to the expression boundaries of the knocked down genes.
source: Recent loss-of-function analyses showed that RNAi of hoxE, hoxD, hoxB, or gbx led to the loss of the pairs of mesenteries corresponding to the expression boundaries of the knocked down genes, while the KD of the putative co-factor of all Hox proteins, Pbx, resulted in the loss of all mesenteries (He et al., 2018) phenocopying the loss of BMP signaling (Genikhovich et al., 2015; Leclère and Rentzsch, 2014; Saina et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to He et al., 2018.

claim: KD of Pbx resulted in the loss of all mesenteries.
source: Recent loss-of-function analyses showed that RNAi of hoxE, hoxD, hoxB, or gbx led to the loss of the pairs of mesenteries corresponding to the expression boundaries of the knocked down genes, while the KD of the putative co-factor of all Hox proteins, Pbx, resulted in the loss of all mesenteries (He et al., 2018) phenocopying the loss of BMP signaling (Genikhovich et al., 2015; Leclère and Rentzsch, 2014; Saina et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to He et al., 2018.

claim: Arp6 is directly suppressed by BMP.
source: Our ChIP and RNA-seq data showed that Arp6 is directly suppressed by BMP (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: Nematostella ZSWIM4-6 is a nuclear protein.
source: Nematostella ZSWIM4-6 is a nuclear protein, whose paralogs, ZSWIM4, ZSWIM5, and ZSWIM6, are conserved in Bilateria.
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data showing nuclear localization.

claim: ZSWIM4, ZSWIM5, and ZSWIM6 are conserved in Bilateria.
source: Nematostella ZSWIM4-6 is a nuclear protein, whose paralogs, ZSWIM4, ZSWIM5, and ZSWIM6, are conserved in Bilateria.
evidence: This is supported by phylogenetic analysis.

claim: In the mouse, the paralogs zswim4-6 were found to be expressed in the forebrain with distinct spatiotemporal patterns.
source: To date, several studies have linked ZSWIM4/5/6 with vertebrate neurogenesis and forebrain development. For instance, in the mouse, the paralogs zswim4-6 were found to be expressed in the forebrain with distinct spatiotemporal patterns (Chang et al., 2020; Chang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chang et al., 2020; Chang et al., 2021.

claim: Zswim6 knockout mice display abnormal striatal neuron morphology and motor function.
source: Zswim6 knockout mice display abnormal striatal neuron morphology and motor function (Tischfield et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tischfield et al., 2017.

claim: zswim4 mutations frequently occur in patients with acute myelogenous leukemia.
source: Additionally, zswim4 mutations frequently occur in patients with acute myelogenous leukemia (Walter et al., 2012), while zswim6 mutations in mammals associate with acromelic frontonasal dysostosis (a rare disease characterized by craniofacial, brain and limb malformations), and schizophrenia (Smith et al., 2014; Tischfield et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Walter et al., 2012.

claim: zswim6 mutations in mammals associate with acromelic frontonasal dysostosis and schizophrenia.
source: Additionally, zswim4 mutations frequently occur in patients with acute myelogenous leukemia (Walter et al., 2012), while zswim6 mutations in mammals associate with acromelic frontonasal dysostosis (a rare disease characterized by craniofacial, brain and limb malformations), and schizophrenia (Smith et al., 2014; Tischfield et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Smith et al., 2014; Tischfield et al., 2017.

claim: zswim4/5 in the frog embryo and zswim4/6 in transit-amplifying mouse hair follicle cells are direct targets of BMP signaling.
source: Interestingly, zswim4/5 in the frog embryo and zswim4/6 in transit-amplifying mouse hair follicle cells are also direct targets of BMP signaling (Genander et al., 2014; Stevens et al., 2017), and zebrafish zswim5 is downregulated in gastrulating bmp7-/- embryos of D. rerio (Greenfeld et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Genander et al., 2014; Stevens et al., 2017.

claim: Zebrafish zswim5 is downregulated in gastrulating bmp7-/- embryos.
source: Interestingly, zswim4/5 in the frog embryo and zswim4/6 in transit-amplifying mouse hair follicle cells are also direct targets of BMP signaling (Genander et al., 2014; Stevens et al., 2017), and zebrafish zswim5 is downregulated in gastrulating bmp7-/- embryos of D. rerio (Greenfeld et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Greenfeld et al., 2021.

claim: Zswim4 attenuates BMP signaling by directly interacting with nuclear SMAD1 and promoting its ubiquitination and degradation in frog embryos and mammalian cells.
source: There, it has been shown that Zswim4 attenuates BMP signaling by directly interacting with nuclear SMAD1 and promoting its ubiquitination and degradation (Wang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2022.

claim: ZSWIM4-6 may have a conserved function as a destabilizer of nuclear SMAD1/5.
source: Our analyses of the effect of the up- or downregulation of the Nematostella zswim4-6 and of the overexpression of the zebrafish zswim5 on the shape of the pSMAD1/5 gradient in these two models appear to be in line with the vertebrate zswim4 data (Wang et al., 2022): ZSWIM4-6 may indeed have a conserved function as a destabilizer of nuclear SMAD1/5.
evidence: This is inferred from experimental data in Nematostella and zebrafish and comparison with vertebrate data (Wang et al., 2022).

claim: Genes known to be negatively regulated by BMP signaling were de-repressed and expanded their expression toward the 'strong BMP signaling side' of the directive axis in spite of the increased levels of nuclear pSMAD1/5 in zswim4-6 KD.
source: We showed that the genes known to be negatively regulated by BMP signaling were de-repressed and expanded their expression toward the 'strong BMP signaling side' of the directive axis in spite of the increased levels of nuclear pSMAD1/5, while the genes positively regulated by BMP signaling were only weakly affected.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization and immunofluorescence data.

claim: Genes positively regulated by BMP signaling were only weakly affected in zswim4-6 KD.
source: We showed that the genes known to be negatively regulated by BMP signaling were de-repressed and expanded their expression toward the 'strong BMP signaling side' of the directive axis in spite of the increased levels of nuclear pSMAD1/5, while the genes positively regulated by BMP signaling were only weakly affected.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data.

claim: ZSWIM4-6 might act as a co-repressor of pSMAD1/5 targets.
source: Together with the results of our ChIP analysis of EGFP-tagged Nematostella ZSWIM4-6 showing that ZSWIM4-6 can bind to the pSMAD1/5 binding site in the upstream regulatory region of one pSMAD1/5-repressed gene, chordin, but not to the pSMAD1/5 binding site in the upstream regulatory region of one pSMAD1/5-activated gene, gremlin, this suggests that ZSWIM4-6 might act as a co-repressor of pSMAD1/5 targets.
evidence: This is inferred from ChIP data showing differential binding to repressed vs activated targets.

claim: ZSWIM4-6 is the first example of a nuclear protein modulating the pSMAD1/5 gradient in a non-bilaterian organism.
source: While the extracellular signaling network setting up the pSMAD1/5 gradient along the directive axis in Nematostella has been addressed before by us and others, ZSWIM4-6 is the first example of a nuclear protein modulating the pSMAD1/5 gradient in a non-bilaterian organism.
evidence: This is based on the novelty of the finding in the context of cnidarian research.
